USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our current pressure posture — allow the already-ordered List 4A tariff to take effect September 1 so we do not lose negotiating credibility — but do NOT escalate further, and pivot firmly into the talks scheduled for early September. Signal conditional willingness to de-escalate (pause/roll back some tariffs) in exchange for verifiable structural commitments on IP, forced technology transfer, and purchases. The leverage is already built; the priority now is to convert it into an agreement rather than add fuel to a recession signal we ourselves are generating.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential (+0.5). The dispute is now materially damaging the U.S. economy and markets: the 10-year yield collapsed ~46% to 1.47% and the yield curve inverted as deeply as 2007 (country_health DGS10/DGS2), consumer sentiment fell 7.6% in a single month to 89.8 (UMCSENT), and the Dow posted its worst day of the year on Aug 14 on inversion fears (NBC/WaPo). With the Fed already easing (FEDFUNDS to 2.13) and Trump campaigning on the economy, a self-inflicted trade recession is the real enemy. Yet the U.S. holds strong leverage — 25% tariffs on ~$250B, the Huawei entity list, the currency-manipulator designation, and List 4A teed up for Sept 1 (event_timeline Aug 1/5/13/23) — so this is not a vulnerability to China but a manageable, market-sensitive escalation. That dual reading drives an action stance just above neutral (+0.1): escalation beyond the already-ordered List 4A would sharply raise recession odds and hurt our own political position, while concession now would squander hard-won leverage with no matched Chinese offer. Negotiating now, with pressure held and a credible de-escalation path on the table, is the correct calibration.

Consumer sentiment collapsed 100→89.8 (-7.6%) in Aug on trade-war headlines
US holds strong leverage: 25% on $250B, Huawei entity list, currency-manipulator designation, List 4A Sept 1

Talks scheduled to resume early September — negotiation window
Further escalation is self-harm: risks a trade-induced recession that undercuts the economy-politics base

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our retaliatory tariffs as a bargaining position but do not escalate further; actively pursue the September round of talks and signal flexible purchase commitments in exchange for relief on List 4 and the Huawei Entity List. A further escalation spiral risks deeper damage to an export economy already showing the worst industrial output in 17 years, while unilateral concession would invite more US pressure — so maintain posture, keep the negotiating lane open, and probe for a rollback in Washington.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is genuinely high and rising. The US has now escalated on every front: List 3 at 25% ($200B, May 10), the Huawei Entity List plus Google/chip-supplier suspensions targeting our flagship firm (May 16-20), a 10% List 4 covering essentially all remaining ~$300B of exports (Aug 1, hiked to 15% on Aug 23), CNY breaking 7 and the currency-manipulator designation (Aug 5), and an explicit order for US companies to decouple (Aug 23). This maps directly to the +0.5 CHN anchor: firm-level targeting (Huawei), FX pressure, and broad export-sector exposure. It is corroborated by real-economic pain — Chinese industrial production grew just 4.8% in July, the worst in 17 years (CNN, Aug 23). This justifies a threat_score near +0.55. It is not existential (+1.0): China retains ~$3T in reserves, capital controls mean no destabilizing outflow, it has stimulus room, and leverage via rare earths, US consumer/agricultural exposure, and the yuan — so +0.55, not +1.0. On action, China's own retaliation ($75B, Aug 23) plus US pain (10-year yield collapsed from 2.7% to 1.47%, UMich sentiment dropped to 89.8, Baa spreads wide, the Aug 14 yield-curve inversion scare) show both sides are absorbing cost, and deputy-level talks were called 'constructive' with principals' talks slated for Washington in September. Escalating further would invite more decoupling pressure at the worst moment for our industrial sector; conceding outright would signal weakness Trump would exploit. The disciplined move is to negotiate — hold retaliation, keep the September lane alive, offer measured purchase commitments only in exchange for real relief.
